title: SPI Windows signing — release design
version_reason: Patch for Windows distribution security. Current stable is 4.4.0; the final version and beta suffix remain controlled by existing release automation. Planned PR: ChatGPT-Fix SPI Windows Authenticode signing [v4.4.1], targeting master without merging it.
problem: The published 4.4.0 portable EXE and x64 installer both report NotSigned in Windows. The ZIP matches GitHub's recorded SHA-256. The build workflow never signs the portable application, installed x64 application, installer or uninstaller. PublisherName in the project is display metadata. PR #112 is already merged and only changes navigation. Existing CI passes without checking signatures. No Actions secrets, variables or environments and no local code-signing certificate were found.
recommendation: Implement an optional certificate-store Authenticode pipeline using a real public-trust certificate with a hardware/cloud-backed private key. Keep signing off until its secure runner, provider and protected environment are configured. Require SHA-256 signing, RFC 3161 timestamps and trusted-identity verification before publishing an enabled signing release. Signing establishes the certificate's publisher identity; SmartScreen reputation remains Microsoft's independent decision.

states.name: Current download: unknown publisher
states.description: Both released EXEs are unsigned. Windows can show Windows protected your PC and Unknown publisher. Existing 4.4.0 files, tags and releases remain historical evidence; this change produces future builds rather than replacing them.

states.name: Signing off: explicit unsigned status
states.description: With signing unconfigured or explicitly off, ordinary hosted CI and beta builds continue. Logs, the version comment and release notes explicitly say unsigned and that the warning is not fixed. No signing key, provider credential or signing runner is available to PR code.

states.name: Trusted release: verified publisher
states.description: After configuration, only an eligible protected-master push uses the isolated signing stage. Windows displays the certificate's validated legal publisher name when trust validation succeeds. An unrecognized-app warning may still appear because signatures do not guarantee reputation. This is an intended state, not a claim that a signed build already exists.

states.name: Signing enabled but invalid: stop publication
states.description: An invalid mode, missing certificate/provider, unexpected signer, untrusted or revoked certificate, failed timestamp, altered binary, missing signature or signing command failure stops publication. There is no silent unsigned fallback. The maintainer repairs the external configuration and reruns normal CI.

states.name: Installer and uninstall: complete coverage
states.description: Sign the final portable EXE after stamping and Costura weaving, and the x64 application before Inno packing. Use Inno's SignTool callback with SignedUninstaller=yes to cover setup, its temporary self-copies and uninstall. Verify the installed application and uninstaller before the existing smoke checks and uninstall.

states.name: External setup required
states.description: The owner must acquire a CA-issued public-trust code-signing certificate, complete identity validation, and use a nonexportable hardware/cloud key with a Windows SignTool-compatible provider. Configure a protected windows-code-signing environment restricted to master, an ephemeral Windows signing runner in a restricted runner group, its provider authentication, the expected certificate thumbprint and a provider-approved RFC 3161 timestamp endpoint. Do not upload a PFX/private key. Microsoft Artifact Signing is a potential later backend only after eligibility is confirmed; its public-trust individual enrollment currently supports US/Canada.

behaviors.trigger: Any PR, including same-repository and fork PRs
behaviors.before: Normal build/test jobs; published same-repository betas are unsigned without a signing status.
behaviors.after: Normal hosted build/test jobs; no signing environment, provider credential or signing runner. Beta output is explicitly unsigned. No pull_request_target signing path.

behaviors.trigger: Protected master push with signing off
behaviors.before: Unsigned release is published with no signature verification.
behaviors.after: Unsigned build is permitted by the optional policy and clearly labelled. No claim of a SmartScreen fix.

behaviors.trigger: Protected master push with certificate-store signing enabled
behaviors.after: A release-only stage signs exact expected EXEs with the configured certificate and SHA-256 RFC 3161 timestamp. It verifies Windows public trust, code-signing usage, the expected signer and timestamp. Publication requires successful verification.

behaviors.trigger: Missing credential or failed signing/verification while enabled
behaviors.after: Fail closed before artifact promotion and publication. Missing or malformed enablement values cannot silently downgrade an enabled release.

behaviors.before: Actions uploads dist/; release job later computes ZIP/installer hashes.
behaviors.after: Preserve updater-compatible portable/ and windows-x64/ contents. Upload final platform contents directly as the named Actions artifact, avoiding a ZIP nested in the artifact download. If the isolated stage needs a temporary handoff artifact, validate its exact run/commit provenance, remove it after promotion or failure, and leave one final downloadable artifact. Keep notices in their existing release/installed locations. Compute ZIP and setup checksums after signatures are final.
Update the expected certificate identity and provider configuration deliberately. Verification fails on an unexpected signer. Document rotation; do not promise transfer of SmartScreen reputation.

saved: No user database profiles, workbooks, rules, passwords or application preferences change. No application UI/navigation changes are included.

Repository configuration stores only a signing mode, runner/environment selection, public certificate thumbprint/store and timestamp URL. Sensitive provider authentication stays in the protected environment or workload identity, with least privilege.
The private signing key remains with the hardware/cloud provider. No PFX import, private key file, credential values or replacement root certificates are committed, logged or packaged.

CI retains nonsecret signing status, signer metadata, final file hashes, event, head SHA and verification results in logs/release evidence. Keep the distributed ZIP payload compatible with existing strict portable updaters.
side_effects: Implementation affects the existing Windows release workflow, shared signing/verification scripts, optional Inno configuration, focused signing tests, release/version status wording and signing documentation. It does not implement absent macOS or Android code.

Secure isolation may require a temporary internal artifact handoff and a narrowly scoped cleanup job with Actions write permission; build/sign jobs retain the minimum permissions needed. The final downloadable artifact remains SPI_Data_Comp_Tool_<version>.zip with platform folders directly inside.

Signing contacts the configured provider and timestamp service; Windows verification may contact certificate/revocation infrastructure. Provider costs, certificate acquisition and identity validation are external owner actions.
Sign before packaging; never change PE resources, versions or embedded libraries after signing. ZIP hashes authenticate download integrity but do not replace Authenticode.
No SmartScreen or Defender settings, execution policies, Mark-of-the-Web data, machine trust stores, merge settings, existing tags or releases are changed. No manual publishing workflow is triggered.
acceptance: Off-mode and PR CI succeed without a certificate; enabled mode fails on incomplete configuration, wrong event/ref, missing files, signer mismatch, absent timestamp, untrusted signatures or tampering. Tests never install a root certificate or weaken machine policy.

Exercise real verification with disposable test fixtures in an isolated test context; self-signed fixtures are never treated as public-trust release signatures. Positive public-trust signing remains explicitly unverified until the external certificate is configured.

For an enabled signed run, verify portable EXE, x64 payload, setup, installed EXE and uninstaller using SignTool /pa /all /v /tw and explicit expected-signer/timestamp checks. Treat warnings, including missing timestamps, as failures.

Run required source tests, layout checks, both Windows builds, assembly checks, installer install/check/uninstall and updater regressions after approval. Test the actual final artifact layout and final signed-byte checksums.

Obtain an independent read-only review; validate the new PR's exact head and associated test-merge CI, not only PR #112's historical green checks. Report real-signing and on-device SmartScreen checks as Not verified while external prerequisites are absent.

Current evidence: PR #112's three applicable workflows passed; the 4.4.0 master Build and checks run 45016856117 passed all five jobs. Neither proves signing. The installed payload and uninstaller from 4.4.0 were not executed or extracted for this audit.

Open the ChatGPT- PR only after approval of this revision. Keep master unmerged; never enable auto-merge, create tags or manually publish releases. The three referenced D:/Projects/Skills/Github Skills policy files are unavailable, so only the supplied policy snapshot could be applied.

alternatives.name: Optional certificate-store pipeline
alternatives.reason: Fits the existing Win32/SignTool/Inno packages and supports a CA/provider appropriate to the validated signer. A hardware/cloud-backed provider can keep the key nonexportable. The owner must provision and restrict its CI runner before enablement.

alternatives.name: Microsoft Artifact Signing with OIDC
alternatives.reason: A strong managed option for eligible identities, but eligibility and an Azure signing account/profile are not established here. Individual public-trust enrollment is currently limited to US/Canada. This revision documents it as an alternative, without pretending credentials exist or adding an unconfigured second backend.

alternatives.name: Microsoft Store MSIX distribution
alternatives.reason: A legitimate alternative with a different packaging/submission/update model. It would require a separate distribution project and does not repair the existing GitHub portable and Inno EXEs within this request.
